 Order

This Criminal Original Petition is filed by the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the defacto complainant to quash the case in CC.No.42 of 2022, for the offences under Sections 498A, 294b,
506(i), 324, 342 and 34 of IPC.
2.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that these petitioners are parents-in-law of the defacto complainant was given a false complaint due to matrimonial dispute with her husband.

3. The learned Government Advocate (Crl.Side) submitted that the complaint is of the year 2017, on completion of investigation final report filed and taken cognizance by the Additional Mahila Court,
Thiruvannamalai in C.C.No.42 of 2022.
The first accused yet to served summons for appearance.
These two petitioners are A2 and A3.
Since there is material to try these petitioners for cognizable offence, the petition to quash is not sustainable.

4. On perusing the records and hearing the submissions made by counsel, this Court is of the view that since the complaint is of the year https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2017, it is suffice to direct the Additional Mahila Court, Thiruvannamalai to expedite and complete the trial within a period of four months provided accused as well as the defacto complainant co-operates in marshalling the witnesses and examining them in chief and cross.

5. As far as these petitioners are concerned, considering the age, the Additional Mahila Court,
Thiruvannamalai shall entertain the petition filed under Section 317 of Cr.P.C for dispensing the personal appearance whenever their appearance is not required for the progress of the trial.
6. With the above observation, this Criminal Original Petition is disposed of.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
The Additional Mahila Court, Thiruvannamalai 2.
The Sub Inspector of Police, AWPS -Thiruvannamalai, Thiruvannamali District 3.
The Public Prosecutor, High Court of Madras, Chennai.
